basis: Visceral diverticula, marfanoid skeletal habitus and retinal detachment characterize this connective tissue syndrome.
ISCU deficiency causes metabolic skeletal myopathy with exercise intolerance and lactic acidosis; singleton blood and ocular findings do not establish common involvement.
Developmental disability and T-cell dysfunction define the syndrome; dental agenesis affects 5/12 (~42%). Asthma is a separately diagnosed disease.
Neoplasm arising in ocular structures; lymphoma is only one subtype of this umbrella.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic sinus disease and bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear disease affects 5/5 patients.
Isolated uterovaginal malformation lies outside the axes; associated urinary abnormalities are very rare.
Loss of external or middle-ear sound transmission defines the disorder.
Persistent hyperkeratotic papules and frequent skin ulceration are confined to the skin.
Mechanical or functional obstruction of the duodenum.
Diabetes caused by pancreatic insulin deficiency; pulmonary and exocrine pancreatic disease belong to underlying cystic fibrosis.
Inherited renal tubular amino-acid transport disorder causing cystinuria; intestinal transport abnormalities do not usually cause digestive damage.
Congenital emphysema, deafness and intellectual disability define the syndrome; the penoscrotal anomaly has no axis.
Carcinoma of the oropharyngeal tonsil; pharyngeal structures belong to the pulmonary axis.
Cold-precipitating plasma fibrinogen disorder; acrocyanosis alone does not establish tissue damage, and persistent renal injury lacks frequency evidence.
Splenic overactivity directly destroys circulating blood cells.
Postural failure of blood-pressure maintenance; an underlying neurologic cause is not universal.
Retinal vascular maldevelopment causes visual impairment and detachment; fractures lack evidence of common involvement in this subtype.
Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia affects skeletal development and joint function.
Selective permanent-tooth agenesis affects all reported patients; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Developmental disability is central; polydactyly and joint hypermobility are frequent (30-79%). Individual cardiac malformations are occasional (5-29%).
Umbrella of neonatal skeletal dysplasias with increased bone density; metabolic disease applies only to particular subtypes.
Cortical malformation and developmental impairment define the disorder; optic atrophy occurs in 1/5, below threshold.
Developmental dental enamel defects impair tooth structure and mastication; extra-dental disease is not common across this umbrella.
Immune dysregulation causes hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; hepatitis affects >50%, STXBP2 enteropathy ~30-40%. CNS involvement omitted under cap; singleton ear/lung findings insufficient.
Complex II metabolic deficiency causes leukodystrophy and spasticity (4/5); hypotonia and motor delay alone do not establish separate skeletal muscle damage.
